shots.target: station 1 deck; base curve g draws itself
The Mix That Cannot Kill a Pole

params.sub: three copies of one curve, weights -1, 3, -2

shots.caption_text: Start with one curve, g. Its height changes as u moves to the right.

shots.target: base curve -> three lane copies (coral, gold, blue)
shots.caption_text: Make three copies of it.

shots.target: gold and blue copies slide by log 2 and log 4; floor brackets
shots.caption_text: Delay the second copy by log 2, and the third by log 4.
Now weight the copies: minus one, three, and minus two.

shots.target: three lanes merge into the ivory sum D
shots.caption_text: Add the three heights at every u. The sum D is the mix.

shots.target: The transform of g has poles. Does any pole survive the mix?
A pole is one pure tone.
coral spiral e^{rho u} grows along the axis
shots.caption_text: A pure tone is a spiral along u. It turns, and it grows.

shots.target: card: rho of the first zeta zero
shots.caption_text: This one is the tone of the first zero of the zeta function.

shots.target: theta -42 -> -78; floor shadow and drop lines
shots.caption_text: Its shadow on the floor is a growing wave.
The curve g is a chord of such waves, one for each pole.
In the transform, this single tone is a pole at s = rho.

shots.target: gold copy slides by log 2; theta -78 -> -40
shots.caption_text: Delay the tone by log 2. The spiral slides along its axis.
A slid spiral is the old spiral times one number, q.

shots.target: phasor plane at u0, seen along the axis
shots.caption_text: Along the axis: q turns the tone 159 degrees and shrinks it to 0.707.

shots.target: three arrows head to tail; card: arrows formula
shots.caption_text: Now the mix. Three arrows, head to tail.
Minus one, then three q, then minus two q squared.
They do not close up. The gap is the number m(rho), 3.98 units long.

shots.target: station 2, oblique; ivory spiral m(rho) e^{rho u} grows
shots.caption_text: So the mix gives back the same tone, 3.98 times larger.
A tone dies only if its own number m(rho) is zero.

shots.target: fly to station 3, resting tilt 24 degrees

shots.caption_text: On the transform side, the whole mix is multiplication by one function, m.
Copy one: no delay, weight minus one. / Copy two: the delay log 2 becomes the factor 2 to the minus s. / Copy three: the delay log 4 becomes 4 to the minus s.

shots.target: symbol terms -> quadratic in q, then its factors
shots.caption_text: Write q for 2 to the minus s. The quadratic in q factors.
This factor is zero only when q is 1.
This factor is zero only when q is one half.
The mix can kill a tone only when q is 1 or 1/2.

shots.target: two circles on the floor; radius formula
shots.caption_text: The size of q depends on one thing only: the real part of s.

shots.target: gold circle shrinks as Re s runs 0 -> 1 -> 1/2, live readout
shots.caption_text: As the real part goes from 0 to 1, the circle shrinks to 1/2.
Inside the critical strip, the real part is strictly between 0 and 1.
So q is strictly between the two circles. It is never on them.

shots.target: kill points q = 1 and q = 1/2 flash
shots.caption_text: And the two kill points? They sit exactly on the circles.

shots.target: annulus becomes a flat three-turn surface

shots.caption_text: Let the imaginary part of s be height. The strip winds into a ribbon.

shots.target: two ember rods and their eight touch points
shots.caption_text: Each kill point becomes a rod. It meets the ribbon only at an edge.
One turn of the ribbon is 9.06 units of height in the strip.

shots.target: the bead rho_1 on the ribbon, with a radial ruler
shots.caption_text: The first zeta zero rides here, in the middle of the ribbon.
Every pole in the strip rides between the edges. No rod can reach it.

shots.target: How much of the tone gets through?
strip floor with its two walls
shots.caption_text: This floor is the strip. Its walls are real part 0 and 1.
Raise each point to the height |m(s)|: how much of that tone passes.

shots.target: six ember zeros on the walls
shots.caption_text: It touches the floor only on the walls, once every 9.06.

shots.target: card: floor inequality; inset graph of the floor
shots.caption_text: Inside, the valleys are low but never zero. Their height has a positive floor.

shots.target: white pillar at rho_1; card: value
shots.caption_text: The first zeta zero stands on a ridge. Its tone passes 3.98 times larger.

shots.target: rise above the floor; residue formula beside the strip
shots.caption_text: Near a pole the transform is r over s minus rho, plus smooth terms.
The pole stays. Its residue becomes m(rho) times r, and m(rho) is not zero.

shots.target: The mix is blind only on the walls.
all five stations in one row
end card: s = 0 removed; s = 1 removed; strip: every pole survives; credit and limit

camera_score: The camera never cuts. It is one flight through five stations, 18 units apart, with a breath of sky between them. In the 3D set pieces (lanes, spiral, ribbon, landscape) it always moves: a slow sideways drift, an orbit, a push toward a bead. Over formulas it goes still and vertical, and it takes each term with the same three steps: whole, part, whole. The slowest move of the film is the dive into 1/2 < |q| < 1; the widest is the last pull-back, where the whole argument stands in one row.
